newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruehe says NATO-Russia treaty ends Cold War era.
newsitem.headline: Ruehe says NATO-Russia treaty ends Cold War era.

text.p: Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said on Monday a landmark treaty between NATO and Russia marked the formal end of the Cold War and closes a chapter of history that began at the Yalta and Potsdam conferences.

Writing a guest column in Tuesday's edition of the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Ruehe said the treaty that will be signed in Paris on Tuesday showed Russia was committed to strategic cooperation with the West as well as economic and political ties.

"The last relicts of the Cold War have been overcome," Ruehe said. "The post-war order established in Potsdam and Yalta are now banished to the history books. The path for a truly cooperative security structure in Europe has now been opened."

The United States and the Soviet Union drafted plans at the Yalta conference towards the end of World War Two and at Potsdam near Berlin immediately after the war that led to the long post-war division of Europe.

NATO leaders headed for Paris on Monday to sign the treaty with Russia intended to lay the basis of a post-Cold War European security order and ease the alliance's expansion into former communist Europe.

Ruehe said: "NATO and Russia are now committed to the same political principles of a peaceful cooperation in Europe -- respecting territorial integrity, the right to freely join an alliance, the commitment to peaceful resolution to disputes, respecting human rights and an opening to democracy and the free market economy."
